bullets.text: HRC at Rs64K/t (+11% since end-July), 3% above import parity; Australian HCC ~US$274/t (+27%); spreads ~1% wider WoW near April peak.
bullets.source: Morgan Stanley — PULSE: India Materials: India Steel Tracker

detail.summary: Domestic prices hold a small premium to import parity, backed by the safeguard duty, so imports should normalise as production ramps. Elevated met coal on China supply disruptions keeps costs high; how spreads evolve beyond monsoon is the stock driver. Medium-term view constructive.
points: Secondary rebar Rs51.7K/t, +2% WoW, +18% since end-July
China CFR iron ore ~US$95/t flat WoW

bullets.source: Kotak — Basic materials - daily news and prices

bullets.text: CLSA expects 2Q cement Ebitda/t down Rs200-250 QoQ despite 7-9% YoY demand growth; preferred picks UltraTech, Shree, Dalmia Bharat.
bullets.source: CLSA — Green Energy Corridor-III | Previews: Banks, Cements | Capex Insights | IDEA

detail.summary: Cement demand beat in 2Q on a below-normal monsoon and resilient housing, but profitability is expected to weaken sharply. CLSA still prefers the three large names into results.

bullets.text: Ambuja (via ACC) commissions 2.4mtpa Salai Banwa grinding unit and 1mtpa Kalamboli blending capacity; consolidated capacity 113.45mtpa; Emkay ADD, TP Rs450 vs CMP Rs374.
bullets.source: Emkay — Cement Corner: Ambuja Cement Commissions 2.4mtpa Salai Banwa GU and 1mtpa Kalamboli GU

detail.summary: ACC commissioned a greenfield grinding unit in Uttar Pradesh and a subsidiary added blending capacity in Maharashtra. Emkay values Ambuja at 15x EV/EBITDA on 1QFY29 and maintains ADD.
points: TP Rs450 vs CMP Rs374, 15x EV/EBITDA

bullets.text: Elara: September cement prices stable QoQ pan-India against usual seasonal softness, South led hikes, West hit by festival headwinds; another price hike scheduled next month.
bullets.source: Elara — Elara Stinger: Centre cuts windfall tax on diesel, ATF exports from October 1 - Monthly Update: Cement (+2 more in Outlook)

detail.summary: Elara's monthly update says partial hikes held through a light monsoon as fuel costs rose, though demand recovery is uneven. Regionally, North leads the recovery and West lags on festival timing.
points: Pan-India prices stable QoQ, breaking seasonal trend
North leads recovery; East, Central mild gains

bullets.text: Coal India Sep e-auction premium jumped to ~94% from ~59% in Aug; Morgan Stanley (OW, PT Rs480) sees upside risk to earnings estimates.
bullets.source: Morgan Stanley — PULSE: Coal India Limited: Sep e-auction premiums at ~94% vs. ~59% in Aug

detail.summary: Sharply higher global thermal coal prices since July and seasonally strong non-power demand are driving premiums. Morgan Stanley sees this as a material positive and expects the stock to do well near term.
points: Premium expected to expand in coming months

bullets.text: Coal India Sep dispatch 61.2mt (+12.5% yoy), production 53.5mt (+9.2%); e-auction premium 94% vs 54% for 1HFY27, 72% allocation.
bullets.source: Kotak — [Kotak] Coal India | Dispatch volumes increased 12.5% yoy in September 2026

detail.summary: Growth leaned on a weak base, and 1HFY27 production is still down. Power-plant stocks at 6.8 days leave room for restocking, while CIL's own stock is ~67mt. Kotak says e-auction earnings likely improved in September.

bullets.text: BofA lifts 2026E copper 3% to US$13,278/t, keeps 2027E US$15,250/t, raises long-term real price to US$12,000/t from US$10,000/t.
bullets.source: BofA — BofA ASIA Daily: U/G BHP to BUY. Copper Upside. (+2 more in Outlook)

detail.summary: BofA expects copper inventories to stay in the US on financing demand and sees supply disruptions as supportive. The higher long-term price drives NAV upgrades; BHP is upgraded to Buy ahead of a November Olympic Dam visit.

bullets.text: ACN FY27 organic guide midpoint 2.25% vs 3% in FY26 implies deceleration; CLSA sees downside risk to FY28 EPS, keeps Hold on TCS/INFY/HCLT/TechM, Wipro Underperform.
bullets.source: CLSA — CLSA: India IT: ACN 4Q26: Steady is enough

detail.summary: ACN beat revenue and EPS by c.3%, but its FY27 organic guide is lower than FY26 growth. Since ACN has been taking share from Indian peers, the guide implies low-single-digit organic growth for them and risk to FY28 EPS.
points: 4Q26 revenue and EPS beat c.3% vs Bloomberg consensus
TCS/INFY valuations at parity to ACN; discount risk in FY28
Hold on TCS, INFY, HCL, TechM; Underperform Wipro

bullets.text: MS expects the ACN-led sentiment lift in India IT to fizzle within weeks unless 2QFY27 revenue prints surprise; macro and pricing unchanged.
bullets.source: Morgan Stanley — India Technology: IT Services: Read-across from ACN's 4QF26

detail.summary: MS sees the ACN beat and FY27 guide as sentiment-positive, but organic growth decelerating at the midpoint, no macro change and hyper-competitive pricing remain concerns for large India IT. Any rally likely fades absent a meaningful 2QFY27 revenue surprise.
points: Uptick in small deals; indirect Middle East impact stabilised
Management: macro unchanged, 4QFY26 pricing lower in many areas
FY27 guide assumes intense competition continues
MS bakes in some F28e organic improvement vs F27e

bullets.text: BofA calls ACN's 7% cc beat largely company-specific, neutral read-across; AI narration constructive (FY27 deflation similar to FY26); prefers Mphasis, Coforge.
bullets.source: BofA — India IT Services: Read across from ACN print: Positive AI narration hits a mark; Q4 beat firm specific - India (+8 more in Outlook)

detail.summary: The beat was driven by smaller deals, faster mobilisation and federal acquisitions, two of them company-specific, with the demand view unchanged and FY27 guide in line. The AI commentary is the sector positive. BofA expects Mphasis and Coforge to stand out in the Sep quarter.
points: Q4 revenue +7% cc yoy vs 3% street
FY27 guide 3-6% cc; 1-3.5% organic; in line
FY27 AI deflation comparable to FY26; token costs falling
FY27 margin expansion guided despite intense pricing competition

bullets.text: CLSA recommends a CRR hike at the 5-7 Oct MPC, with or without a repo hike that OIS already prices as near-certain.
bullets.source: CLSA — CLSA: India Economics: MPC Preview: Why not a CRR hike?

detail.summary: CLSA says a repo hike is almost a given per OIS, but would achieve little amid the current liquidity surplus. A CRR hike, though seen as taboo, has definite benefits, so CLSA recommends it next week.
points: CLSA calls for CRR hike, with or without repo

bullets.text: Nifty fell 3.1% last week, an eighth straight weekly loss (longest since 2001); forward PE 16.9x, lowest since June 2022.
bullets.source: CLSA — CLSA: India strategy: Weekly wrap

detail.summary: The Nifty's losing streak is the longest since 2001 and has taken valuations to a four-year low. FIIs kept selling, the 10-year yield rose, and CLSA's Bull-Bear index stays bearish.
points: FIIs sold US$2.5bn equities; CY26-TD outflows US$27.9bn
Bond-earnings yield gap 1.3ppts vs c.1ppt average

bullets.text: MSCI India fell 6.9% in September, as Brent +14% m/m and DM hikes lifted the 10-year yield 24bps; FIIs sold $3.2bn.
bullets.source: JPM — India Equity Strategy: September 2026 wrap: Global rate hikes and crude spike outweigh resilient domestic prints (+2 more in Outlook)

detail.summary: September's drop came from crude and global rate hikes, with a weaker rupee and primary-market supply adding pressure. Domestic prints stayed resilient: industrial output and trade deficit beat expectations.

bullets.text: Sep wholesales beat ex-Bajaj: Maruti +24.4%, TVS +24.3%, Tata CV +42.4%; Bajaj 9% below estimate; M&M tractors -21.2% on El Nino.
bullets.source: PhillipCapital — India Auto Wholesales Analysis - Sept-2026 | Healthy growth (ex-tractors) despite delayed festivals! | Entering normalized era

detail.summary: Pre-festive build and retail traction lifted September wholesales above estimates, except Bajaj, hit by production and shipping issues. Tractors are de-growing on a high base and El Nino. Retail growth should moderate to mid-to-high single digits in Navratri-Diwali as the GST-cut base rises.
points: Normalised industry growth of 7-8% expected from Q4FY27

bullets.text: Sep registrations: 2W +39%, PV +44%, CV +41% YoY on a GST-cut base; growth to moderate to mid-single digits from October.
bullets.source: CLSA — CLSA: India autos: Auto barometer

detail.summary: September retail was strong across segments, largely because the first three weeks of Sep 2025 were subdued ahead of the 22 Sep GST cut. The base effect starts hitting from next month, so YoY growth moderates, but absolute momentum is expected to hold. Wholesale outpaced retail, implying channel stocking ahead of festivals.
points: TMPV volumes +65% YoY; MSIL lost 180bps share
Top picks: M&M, Bajaj Auto, TVSL, Ather

bullets.text: HEG Graphite EBITDA/t seen rising from ~US$700 in Q1FY27 to US$1,200-1,400 in FY28E as CY27 contracts reset; demerged entity lists within weeks.
bullets.source: Aditya Birla Capital — HEG Graphite (NOT RATED) | Darwin's test passed; spread expansion yet to be priced in (+5 more in Outlook)

detail.summary: After a day at HEG HQ, the broker sees the company surviving the graphite electrode downturn with the strongest cost position and a 100ktpa single-site plant. Stock gains reflect value unlock and early recovery hopes; spread expansion arrives with a lag as offtake contracts roll over, and is not yet priced.
points: FY28E EBITDA/t US$1,200-1,400 as CY27 pricing resets higher
Plant capacity 100ktpa at a single site
HEG Graphite to list in coming weeks after demerger
